paragraphs: Children in care in Hampshire are looked after by Hampshire County Council's own service, Fostering Hampshire Children, and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. In July 2025 the council said it needed to find 150 new fostering households by the end of 2026.

The council looks for carers for children of every age, from babies to teenagers, as well as brothers and sisters who need to stay together and children with additional needs or disabilities. It offers short-term and long-term fostering, emergency and out-of-hours care, respite breaks and parent and child placements. It has also appealed for carers who can offer a home to young people who have arrived in the UK alone seeking refuge.

To apply to the council you need to be over 21 and have a spare bedroom. You do not need to own your home or have worked with children before. Carers receive training, their own supervising social worker and access to the Hampshire Hive, a local network that aims to give fostering families the feel of an extended family. The council says its allowances are competitive but does not publish the figures in its news releases, so ask for the current rates when you enquire.

Agencies set their own fees and support, so it is worth speaking to the council and two or three of the agencies below, and asking each about training, out-of-hours help and what they pay, before you choose.
